chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from the one who mentioned him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Cursed is the one who delays the Maghrib prayer; he seeks its superiority."

key_terms.مَلْعُونٌ: Cursed (one who is under God's curse)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on delaying the Maghrib prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the curse upon delaying Maghrib to the specific intent of seeking 'fadl' (superiority or precedence), likely referring to prioritizing it over the prescribed time or gaining undue spiritual merit. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *ta'khir* (delaying within the valid window) versus *ta'khir* (missing the time), underscoring that ritual timing is not merely mechanical but tied to the worshipper's intention and adherence to the Prophet's tradition.
